long_biography.plain_text:
Jean Lemire first saw the sea at nineteen, during a visit to the Mingan Islands. He had gone out to look for birds, but the sight of a blue whale changed the direction of his life. The encounter drew him towards marine research and a career bringing the ocean’s wildlife to wider audiences.

His Antarctic expedition placed scientists and filmmakers together for 430 days, including a winter in the polar environment. Their work became Le dernier continent and a television series exploring the effects of climate change. Satellite and internet connections allowed students in hundreds of schools to follow the expedition. The research thus reached classrooms while it was happening, making the vulnerability of distant marine ecosystems part of an immediate educational experience.
